videos.teaches: Unity and 0.91-lagging targets; input S/P/Q, unchanged active power, capacitor var, current, reactance, µF and new supply current.
videos.flowRationale: Two sequential board examples, beginning with the motor branch and ending with the capacitor and corrected supply; no new complex-number prerequisite.
videos.qualification: Examples use 120 V, 60 Hz. Use the question’s voltage/frequency; if shaft output is given, first use electrical input = shaft output/efficiency. Correction reduces supply current; motor-branch current and working kW do not automatically fall.
videos.limits: Shaft-output/efficiency conversion is supplied by the existing motor-input lesson, not demonstrated in this video. Auto-captions drop zeros/decimal points; independently recomputed examples agree after rounding.

videos.teaches: Schematics to a four-step delta bank, CT/voltage feedback, contactors, relative 1:2:2:2 steps, target PF, delay/deadband and changing load.
videos.flowRationale: Brief course introduction, then the actual schematic, equipment connections, controller settings and observed switching.
videos.qualification: The bench uses 45/90 var steps. Controller CT scaling changes displayed current/power units; those settings are not installation ratings. Use actual CT/bank data and keep discharge/switching delays appropriate to the equipment.
videos.limits: Training demonstration rather than a complete motor-feeder design from the exact 5/10/25 kVAr paper brief. Controller scaling and acceptance deadband are equipment-specific.

videos.teaches: Thyristor-controlled reactive support using reactors, capacitors and a control system.
videos.flowRationale: Short visual identification of the three functional parts; follows the existing condenser introduction.

videos.teaches: Conventional stator, wound rotor, brushes/slip rings, resistor bank, starting-current/torque benefit, resistance removal, cost/maintenance and inefficient resistance speed control.
videos.flowRationale: Physical rotor and a simple hand-drawn circuit before start/run behaviour and trade-offs; follows cage and torque foundations.
videos.qualification: External resistance is reduced as the motor accelerates. The quoted torque percentages and NEMA comparisons are examples, not universal values; resistance adjustment does not itself change the winding inductance.
videos.limits: No universal torque percentage or actual resistor-bank sizing; North American design labels are comparisons.

videos.teaches: Resistance-split-phase, capacitor-start and capacitor-start/run; phase angle versus starting torque, run-capacitor PF benefit, centrifugal switch, dual-voltage wiring and reversal.
videos.flowRationale: Construction and phase shift before successive capacitor arrangements, then connections; builds on the existing single-phase lesson.

videos.teaches: Pulsating field and no initial net torque, auxiliary phase shift, start capacitor/switch and the shaded ring producing a travelling flux component with low starting torque.
videos.flowRationale: Observed no-start symptom, winding sketch, capacitor/switch demonstration, then a physically opened shaded-pole fan.
videos.qualification: Treat the hand-started motor as a concept demonstration; do not hand-start an energised machine. Shaded-pole motors have low starting torque. Start/run capacitor duty and the manufacturer’s diagram remain essential.
videos.limits: Demonstration is not a safe site test procedure. Does not replace the preceding explicit run-capacitor/PF comparison.

videos.teaches: DC field versus AC stator, slip rings, constant synchronous speed, load/torque angle, pull-out, starting methods, V/inverted-V behaviour and measured lagging/unity/leading operation.
videos.flowRationale: Explicit induction comparison, rotor construction, operational limits and field control, then repeated measured tests to verify the theory.
videos.qualification: Speed stays synchronous while the motor remains in step. Field excitation changes reactive power and pull-out capability; the 60 Hz laboratory values are examples. Deliberate loss-of-step tests are supervised demonstrations.
videos.limits: Longer foundation; some informal humour. Does not teach hunting; the separate specialist lesson follows. Technical knowledge is taken from explanation, not from reproducing destructive tests.

videos.teaches: Hunting/phase swinging, damped versus undamped load-angle graphs, shaft/current/heating effects, load/supply/field/torque disturbances and mitigation.
videos.flowRationale: Focused definition → graph → effects → causes → damping, after the new synchronous-motor foundation.
videos.qualification: Hunting is transient oscillation about the operating load angle. The 0–2δ graph is an idealised load-step illustration, not a universal amplitude. Damper windings reduce oscillations; steady synchronous speed does not exclude temporary speed deviations.
videos.limits: Only India-based addition: no suitable UK or other non-India English-caption lesson was found after the recorded broader search. English original/default audio and English ASR are verified; no Hindi or English auto-dub was accepted. Damper physical construction is introduced in the preceding foundation.

videos.teaches: Magnetic holding, Start/Stop, supply-failure release, no automatic restart on supply return and comparison with contactor/auxiliary three-phase control.
videos.flowRationale: Working switch, isolated teardown and explicit restart scenario; follows the complete DOL circuit rather than introducing coils prematurely.

videos.teaches: Power circuit, coil/holding circuit, interlocks, Stop/overload, manual Start/Run, speed transition, open-transition current and correct rotation.
videos.flowRationale: Physical voltage/connection rationale before labelled primary and ladder diagrams; walks every contact change. Sets up the timer sequel.
videos.qualification: This first circuit uses separate Start/Run commands; the next lesson automates changeover. Y means star. Six- and twelve-lead North American examples require the motor to be delta-rated at the available running supply.
videos.limits: Does not yet automate changeover; requires the next lesson. Transition spikes are load/motor/timing-dependent, not guaranteed below DOL in every case.

videos.teaches: On-delay contacts, holding and reset; fully traced timed star–delta Start/Stop/overload/interlock circuit, followed by soft-starter run/bypass/brake timing.
videos.flowRationale: Explains timer behaviour through simple examples before adding timed contacts to the previously taught star–delta circuit.
videos.qualification: Timed star–delta control follows the introductory on-delay examples. Star and delta must be interlocked with a suitable break-before-make interval; timer and overload settings depend on the actual starter and motor.
videos.limits: Includes resistor/part-winding/soft-starter examples as timer applications, not newly declared C1 compulsory motor types. Device-specific wiring and certified protective settings remain manufacturer work.

videos.teaches: No-start decision path through free shaft/load, overload, wiring, motor-terminal voltage, fuse/switch/contact losses and windings; then speed, heating, noise and phase loss.
videos.flowRationale: Symptoms lead to ordered checks rather than immediately replacing the motor; consolidates the existing phase-loss and isolated-winding test lessons.
videos.qualification: Isolate and prove dead before mechanical or dead tests. No-load current and cable-length examples are not universal limits. Trace voltage loss under the actual load, establish the cause before resetting protection, and verify the repair.
videos.limits: Narrated workflow, not a complete on-site live test/repair/recommissioning demonstration. One-third no-load current and 50 ft cable comments are not universal and are explicitly qualified.
